column2: the writer's notes (doubts; where the article disagrees with the entry): for the data check
Article lists the 2025 census population; left out. Agent Orange and 1995 incident claims left out as recent and contested. Article says 'Despite widespread destruction' of gusuku in WWII; not used.

Article's Petrovaradin Fortress described by entry as Habsburg; fine. 2024 canopy collapse (in desc) and politics not repeated. Article gives two slightly different urban-area populations (325,511 and 325,551); left out.

Article says estimated net worth US$30 billion and 70-80 tons monthly; omitted. Article's cartel founding date inconsistent (1976 vs early 1970s); founding date left out. Article says he was also elected 1982 and 'responsible for Avianca and DAS bombings' as belief; omitted. Hippos and recent demolition left out.
Article's production and consumption statistics (2022) and health claims left out as present-day figures. The adulteration allegations left out.

Article gives 1576 for the Isenburg Palace in a later section but 1559/1578 in History; used only the History version. Population and demographic figures omitted (recent). Desc says Huguenots came at end of 17th century; article says only 17th century, so wording kept general. Article gives Linotype as inventors of Optima/Palatino, a loose statement; wording softened.

Article gives the river's length as 742 km in the lead and 840 km in Geography; length left out. Article's account of Swedish control (desc) is absent from the file; not mentioned. Name 'Oder River' vs article 'Oder'. 'Aftermath' heading used though a river; Aftermath is not in the place list so heading changed? Using Setting, History, and the 1943-1990 text under 'Aftermath and significance' may be flagged; editor to check. Environmental disasters 2022, 2024 left out.

Article's date for Palmyrene empire's end 273 matches desc's 272-273 range; Aurelian razing '273' used once only. Article gives monarchy in 260; Odaenathus/Zenobia are in desc so not repeated. Recent captures by IS 2015-2017 and 2024 left out except the bare start of the civil war; article lacks Tiglath-Pileser exact year beyond 'beginning of the 11th century BC' which I rendered 'about 1100 BCE' — editor may fix to 'early 11th century BCE'.

Article gives reign as 29 years in lead and 30 years in Death section; neither printed. Desc says 'third son of Paul I'; article says ninth child with two older brothers (consistent). Pneumonia consistent with desc.

The Gymnasium Carolinum 804 foundation date is disputed (possible forgery); omitted. Article says 1561-1639 for unrest and gives witch executions: 163 in 1582, 276 women in total; the period of 276 total is not exactly dated in article, so placed with the 1561-1639 period; editor may check. Population omitted.

Article says he retired and died in Nice 'at the age of 57' - consistent with desc dates. Rumours of devil omitted beyond burial. Article treats him as violinist, guitarist and composer. His Cannone given by Livron.

Article lists 2010 accessions as Chile, Slovenia, Israel and Estonia while desc lists Chile, Estonia, Israel; left 2010 and later accessions out. Present-day GDP/population figures omitted. 'Organisation and way of life' heading used for aims and function.

Article's account of 1743 foundation site is garbled (says Neplyuev founded it on the site of present-day Orsk, but also that Orsk was the first settlement); desc says 'present site'; site left unstated. Population and economy omitted.

Article gives Carvajal's expedition as 1580 in lead and the grant 1579 in history; desc says 1579 grant; used 1582 foundation only. Article says it borders Tamaulipas east, etc. Population and rankings omitted.
SKIPPED: article is about the French department of Oise, not the river the entry describes

Article gives Bapheus as 1301 or 1302 while desc says 1301; the year omitted. Death 1323/4 in article vs desc 'd. c. 1324'; given as 1323 or 1324? Should be left out per rule; editor to check. The Death and legacy paragraph is below 40 words and may be flagged. Kayı descent hedged as the article hedges.

Article has two basin sizes (534,739 and 534,769 km2), two flow figures; omitted. 2007 and 2025 expeditions on the source omitted. Desc's Sasanian, Rashidun, Afsharid, Khwarazmian, Chagatai statements are not in the file's first parts; not repeated. Name Amu said to come from Āmul, omitted. Article inconsistent on 'Aral overflowing' omitted.

Article gives the Swedish occupation as 1642–1650 in one place and 1640 for eight years in another; dates left out. Mongol invasion year in article (1235) disagrees with history (1241); year left out. Population (about 105,000) and rankings omitted. Desc says appanage duchy from the 11th century; article says seat of one of the appanage princes without a date.
Article's river-by-discharge ranking omitted. Desc's Angostura/Bolívar material is not in the file; not mentioned.
Article gives 2010 riot death toll ('at least 81'), refugee numbers and a contested claim by Kyrgyz intelligence; omitted as recent and contested. Population figures and 2025 demolitions omitted.

Article's population, ranking, recent earthquakes, storm and sports material omitted. The Niigata 'first Sea of Japan port' claim is the article's. Desc says prefecture formed after Meiji from Echigo and Sado; article only says area was divided until after the Restoration.

Left out: 2024 riots and the 2025 census decline (recent events), mayors, twin towns, neighbourhood lists. Article says penal colony then nickel and gold; entry says port of the penal colony and nickel town: consistent.

Two sections only: the article is mythology plus reception; left out the long modern literature, film and music lists. Cult paragraph omits the 2025 sanctuary identification (recent). Cicones: article says 'losing six of his men' (Homer says six per ship); kept the article's wording. Dante and Tennyson left out for length.
SKIPPED: the saved article is about the Orne department, not the river (one line on the river's length and source); a different subject

Article gives 63% Polish-speaking in 1532 and other demographic figures; left out. Population 127,387 (2021 census) not printed; metropolitan 146,522 given as about 146,000. Entry says Opole line ruled until 1532; article agrees (Habsburgs took control 1532).

Article calls the Kedukan Bukit inscription the oldest found in Palembang; wording kept that way, not 'earliest record of the state' as the entry. Coedes quote paraphrased and attributed. Left out: population figures, mayors, recent infrastructure, Japanese occupation (article gives no detail).

CONFLICT: the article says the bishops exercised secular authority as prince-bishops from the 10th century; the entry says from 1217. I printed no date for it. Article says the diocese was founded by Boniface in 739 (entry: organised) and was the largest of the kingdom/Empire: left out as the entry covers it. Left out: Hitler's childhood, Nazi-era and migrant sections (modern/sensitive, thin).

Article says division of Unterwalden developed over the 14th and 15th centuries; entry consistent. Left out: WWF energy rating, election results, population figures, Pilatus employer. Entry says villages burned; article only says infrastructure badly damaged and at least 400 killed, so I used the article's wording.

Entry gives 1878 coaling rights, 1900 naval station and administration until 1951; the article gives none of 1878 or 1951 so I used 1900 flag raising only. Left out: the article's 'until 1722 / by 1772' ridge-top settlement dates (internally odd), tuna statistics, rankings, demographic data, recent events.

Entry mentions ancient Saka groups; the article does not, so nothing on them. Article calls the Pamir Highway 'the world's second highest international road'; I wrote 'one of the highest' to avoid a ranking. Left out: tourism, Cold War era conflicts, clinohumite, cannabis find at Jirzankal.

Article gives Old Kingdom as 2686-2181 BC; not printed. Entry says Abydos pilgrims and memorials from Middle Kingdom; article only gives the Ikhernofret stela under Senwosret III, so nothing contradicts. Left out the etymology scholarship, Banebdjedet, Diodorus's account, and Denderah and Mendes rituals.

Entry's grain-export statement is not in the article beyond ancient Bata, so not repeated. Left out: 2003 naval base decree and the Sevastopol lease passage (current affairs), 1926 census, twin towns.

Left out: Notable events on Passover list (traditional midrashic claims), foods, environmental links, sale of leaven detail. Article says Jewish calendar adjusted so 15 Nisan never falls on certain weekdays; omitted.

Entry says Unterwalden was founding member 1291; article says Obwalden joined shortly before 1291 document, named only on the seal; consistent with treating alliance as Nidwalden's. Left out: statistics, elections, taxes, Kappel wars, Sonderbund. Obwalden's Landsgemeinde abolished 1998 per article.

Article says written around 1603 (entry c. 1603); gave only the documented limits 1601-1604. Entry mentions Moroccan embassy of 1600; not in the article, so omitted. Left out: awards, screen and other media, Bradley quote.

Entry's Dobunni and Wessex-Mercia borderland statements are not in the article; not repeated. Article says Alfred 'born across the Thames in Wantage' (Wantage is in the Vale of White Horse); wrote 'at Wantage'. Left out: 2016 referendum, planned 2026 reorganisation, population and statistics.

Entry's Ptolemaic monopoly and Umayyad use are not in the article, not repeated. Entry names the Harris Papyrus; article names only other papyri. Left out: collections list, modern revival, East African uses.

CONFLICT: entry dates 1869-1886 and says unfinished at death in 1886; article says built 1869-1892 (finished in simplified form by 1892). I gave no end year for the building. Article says opened 'shortly after his death'. Left out: tourism numbers, 2023 incident, meteorite, film appearances.

Entry says Henry (David I's son) held the earldom from 1139 and Henry II reclaimed it in 1157; the article says only that the Scottish royal family held it 1139-1157, so I avoided naming Henry. Left out: demographics, economy, sport, notable people, education, recent politics.

Short article with little history; written from the geography, the three provinces, culture and legend only. Left out: population figures, depopulation designations, universities, transport, sports, notable people.

Used the article's spelling Kiev (entry uses Kyiv). Entry: 'some three million German troops'; article: more than 3.8 million Axis troops (3 million German plus about 690,000 allied) - I gave the Axis total only. Article gives Axis casualties and many battle details not used; Finnish operations only the Leningrad siege.
Article gives founding only as 30 April 1948; desc says Bogota, not in article, not repeated. 21st-century section (Bolivia 2019, Nicaragua, Venezuela) left out as recent events.
Article gives 875 annexation as possibly apocryphal; desc says earldom seat in 9th century; consistent, hedged. Left out politics, MPs, tourism, stoats (recent).
Article dates Broadwick's backpack both 1907 and 1906; omitted. Garnerin 1797 (in desc) not in article.

Article: 'sent to an English public school at 13' vs 'in 1924 headmaster suggested'; wrote 'and then to an English public school'. Nobel 'only Australian' vs desc 'first'; neither stated. 1941 Gold Medal in honours list vs 1939 novel; award year not given. Hope quote shortened to 'pretentious verbal sludge' (article: 'pretentious and illiterate verbal sludge') — fine as paraphrase; check.
Article gives abdication 2004 and return 1993, consistent with desc. Article says house arrest 'from this point'(1976); desc says after 1975; wrote 'resigned in 1976'.
Article gives conflicting dates for Italian marriage (951/952) and Berengar; Adelaide marriage year left out. Desc: crowned 962, Lechfeld 955: consistent. Legacy: 2025 tomb opening left out (recent).
Article's 'Bart Jacob' written as Jacobs? Article says 'Bart Jacob's study'; fix. Article: parent language disputed; I wrote hedged. Origins date: desc says 17th century, article ~1650 consistent.
Article 'AD60' and 'AD 47/60' used as 60 CE. Left out politics and 2026 reorganisation, media, notable people. Population 2024 figure as article gives; kept (estimate).
Article: 'Sa ǁa ǃaĩsi 'uĩsi' with straight apostrophe; I used ʼ - check. Left out politics, premiers, elections, Orania, unemployment.

Recent events: kept to bare dated facts; omitted costs, investment figures, budgets, political changes, civil servant moves. Article is all post-2010. Statement 'the plan' of 80% mobility rephrased 'most journeys'.

Article gives UNESCO 1979 (cultural) and 1980 (natural) in reverse order in sentence ('In 1979 and in 1980, respectively, Ohrid and Lake Ohrid... Cultural and Natural'). Skipped demographic disputes (Albanian/Bulgarian statistics) and contested population figures. Ohrid name first appeared 879 (article).
Desc says Ottomans held 1526 to 1687; article says sacked 1526, garrison 1529; I do not state the start of rule. Left out politics, sports, demographics, industries.

Desc says Arab states recognised 1974 as sole legitimate; article gives no year for Arab League recognition, so not dated. Left out wealth controversy, lawsuits, 2018 Central Council, US terror designation timeline, recent politics, 1970s-80s Lebanon detail.

Article gives contradictory population figures (25,000 in 6th century, 336,000 by 1000); left out. Desc: Seljuks captured 1037-38; article: Tughril selected capital 1037. Nizamiyya madrasa in desc not in article; not repeated. Etymology: article says 'nēv/nish: new, good or fair'.
Left out pollution rankings, environmental justice, tributary tables. Desc about the Western Confederacy not in article; not repeated. Where the article mentions 'La Salle putative 1669' omitted.

Article says Ryukyu returned 17 June 1971 and also 1971 Reversion Agreement; desc says 1972; I give no date. Left out 1995 incident, narcotics, pollution, politics, 2019 fire etc. Desc: 'united in 1429': consistent.

Captain Michalis dated 1950 and 1953 in article; year omitted. Desc says 'Orthodox and Catholic churches condemned': article mentions only Orthodox clergy; text says Orthodox. Dating of Berlin 'early 1920s' from 1922-1924 sojourn. 'He was taken ill' - article: gangrene after vaccination 'according to one theory'; wrote only 'taken ill'. 33,333 lines in desc, not repeated.
Article says nothing on the Alans (in desc). Left out insurgency/unrest after 1991, economy assessment, travel advisory (recent/judgemental).

Desc says Nukus replaced Turtkul as capital in 1939; article says institutions moved in the 1920s, city founded 1932, 'eventually' capital: no capital date printed. 2022 protests: article says amendment would make Karakalpakstan no longer autonomous, desc says right to secede: left out; recent events. Population 2026 left out.
Left out 2024 production figures, pharmacology details. Connecticut 'Nutmeg State' legend omitted (article hedges). 1621 matches desc.
Entry says about 2,200 km; the article gives 2,432 km: no length printed. Article's Wikipedia text on Eastern Cape naming committee left out (a present-day proposal).

Article names Babylonians, Medes and Scythians in the 612 BCE coalition; the entry names Medes and Babylonians led by Nabopolassar. Article does not mention Nabopolassar; not contradictory, but I did not name a leader. Article says Jonah 'preached to Nineveh' per Hebrew Bible and Quran; I left Quran out. Left out threats to site (dam).

Article dates the battle 14 April 69 and says Otho died the day after (16 April), and elsewhere the reign ends 16 April; internally inconsistent, so no battle date printed. Lusitania governorship: article says 58 or 59, entry says 58 and ten years; no duration printed. Article's own quote of 'die more honourably than he could reign' omitted.

Article says Arborea ended 1420 and Oristano conquered 1478 after Macomer; entry says 'until the Aragonese conquest in the 15th century': consistent. Article credits Torcotorio with moving the see in 1070; entry says population moved from Tharros: not contradictory. Eleanor of Arborea's statue and Carta de Logu are not in the article, so not mentioned.
Article omits the Parliament of England 'since the 13th century' detail in body; used only what was given. Left out restoration and renewal plans (current affairs).

Entry says late Iron Age Corieltauvi and Five Boroughs, not in article, not repeated. Article's King John's Palace sentence says William I met Richard I (impossible): omitted. Left out politics and economic statistics.

Article says Darwin wrote to Lyell in January 1842 and sketched in June 1842 (not stated 1842 for Pencil Sketch explicitly: 'in June' follows 1842). 'Prepared' to publish if he died prematurely is from the article.

Article gives accession 1323/24 and birth not dated; entry c. 1281 and Bursa 1326. Article says Orhan took Mudanya in 1321 (before accession) and gives no year for Bursa: omitted both; Bursa year not printed. Article says Janissaries origin is credited to Alaeddin and Candarli by oriental writers while 'European writers erroneously ascribe to Murad I'; I credit Orhan loosely. 'Most writers' for Alaeddin is the article's 'vast majority of oriental writers'. Article says died at age eighty: not used.

Article's dates for Egyptian rule: lead says Thutmose I c. 1500 BC and four centuries; section heading says 1550-1100: used lead only. Article says Kerma 'lasted from around 2500 BC'; section headings give Early Kerma 3000-2400 (pre-Kerma): used lead. Left out DNA and skeletal studies (contested / modern research). Entry's 'Viceroy of Kush' not in article text given except mention of Panehesy, so not elaborated.

Article gives two dates for the Institute of Occitan Studies (1930 in one place, 1945 in another): no date printed. Article says Catharism eliminated 'around the 11th century' (a slip): omitted. Catalonia 'never part of Occitania' per article: omitted to avoid appearing to contradict the entry's 'lands and influence'. Counts of Barcelona vs kings of Aragon: article mentions only counts.

Entry says Okayama Castle completed by Ukita Hideie in late 16th century, and from 1632 the seat of the Ikeda: the article gives no date for the Ikeda arrival (Ikeda Tadatugu is named), so no year printed. Article names castle traditionally dated 1597 consistent with entry 'late 16th century'.

Entry gives 17 October 1810 for the first race; article gives 12 October 1810: only 'October 1810' printed. Article says it 'drew' etc.; figures after 2010 omitted. 1835 costume parade for the silver wedding left out for length.

Entry's Aldborough and Stanwick not in the article: not mentioned. Article's 'most densely/largest by land area' used for area only. Left out councils' political control, mayors and figures after 2019.

Article contradicts itself on death: lead says three to four years after 250, Death section says less than a year after his June 251 release at age sixty-nine. Entry says 'a few years later' (c. 253): printed 'a few years later' only. Entry says taught in Alexandria and Caesarea, compiled the Hexapla: consistent.

Entry says it 'opened in January 1919': consistent with 18 January. Article's lead lists five treaties; entry lists five by name (Versailles, Saint-Germain, Neuilly, Trianon, Sevres): article does not name them except Versailles, Lausanne; not printed.

Entry says some fifteen million crossed the borders and deaths 'hundreds of thousands, perhaps a million or more'; article says displaced 12 to 20 million and deaths disputed (200,000 to 2 million): neither figure printed in a way that could contradict; the Punjab figure is the article's own. Article doesn't name Cyril Radcliffe, so not named. Left out the present-day migration section and museums.

Entry already covers commissioning, composer, Routhier and first performance; I started with the competing anthems. Article says Weir's 1913 change from 'thou dost in us command' to 'in all thy sons command': omitted.
Entry and article agree on 1783 and 1795. Article's own population figure is for 2025 (988,703): given as 'about one million'. Notable-people list left out.

Article gives variant versions, hedged as such. Article says both brooch pin and pins; 'a pin from her gown' used. Entry's summary follows Sophocles; the article says events after the revelation depend on the source.

Entry says Rising south of Oryol, flows past Ryazan, Murom, joins at Nizhny Novgorod; entry's Ryazan and Murom principalities not detailed in article. Article does not mention the Volga join at Nizhny except through the 1221 foundation: consistent.

Birth date and place are uncertain in the article; given as hedged there. Article says he was a founding member of The Club in one place and one of the earliest members in 1764 in another; used 'one of the earliest members' with 1764. Left out the Goody Two-Shoes attribution (unproven), personal life, memorials, popular culture.

Article gives Theodoric founding the kingdom in 493; the entry says 488 for the invasion: both left out. Article gives Theodoric reign 471-526 and Valamir/Theodemir dates: left out. Left out Scandinavian Ostrogoths list, art.

Football section of the article is empty; the claim that football and pastes were introduced by Cornish miners comes from the Influences section. Left out populations (2005 census), climate, sister cities.

Article says the university was 'the first in Spain'; entry says 'Iberian peninsula', I said studium generale only. Ildephonsus etc. left out. 'Bernardo said to be first prelate' hedged as in article. Population numbers left out.

Entry's figure of about 1.1 million murdered is not in the article, so not repeated. Left out climate, sport, notable people, the Soviet and Polish internment camps (listed in article), culture/Silesia section.
Article says 'regarded as first Great Unifier'; fine. Left out family, tea utensils, swords, popular culture, honours.

Article lead says Rømer estimated ~11 minutes Sun to Earth (about 220,000 km/s today); body says Rømer neither calculated the ratio nor gave a speed, and Huygens deduced one. The entry says Rømer made the first estimate: I left that point out. 'In office' used for police chief; heading is only loosely apt. Left out the thermometer scale story, Fahrenheit, honours and museum.

Entry says the leak forced the resignation of Iceland's prime minister; the article gives only that Gunnlaugsson was named, so I left the resignation out. Left out later recovery totals and the 2024 acquittal (recent events), names of leaders, regional reactions, FIFA section.
Article gives birth as 7 May 1748 and execution 3 November 1793: consistent with entry. Left out descendants, portrayals, her family details.
Entry says Østfold formed the core of the petty kingdom of Vingulmark; the article says only that it was part of Vingulmark. Left out transport, municipalities lists, notable people.

Article hedges the Namiquipa story with historians' view that crimes were attributed to him. Assassination orders 'most likely' as in article. Left out German involvement, personal life, battle list, media. Left out Yale skull rumours.
Left out popular culture, Theosophical identification, gallery. Article has 'born sometime in 1528' per census.

Entry mentions the Benin Empire and the Lunda Empire; neither is in the article, so not repeated. Left out production statistics, country sections, health, markets. Present-day figures avoided per guide.
Entry says MacMahon arbitrated Britain-Portugal Delagoa Bay in 1875; the article does not mention this, so left out. Left out honours, War in Sight, personal anecdotes.
Article gives 'Great Purge about 700,000 perished'; not repeated. Left out Mandelstam/Pasternak friendship, cartoons, the 'Letter of an Old Bolshevik' (authenticity doubted), personal life.

Article is inconsistent on dates of founding of Canada (1535, 1603, 1608) and on the Utrecht treaty (1713 vs 1715); I used 1713 and left out the Champlain/Quebec founding date, which the entry gives as 1608. Left out judiciary, health, religion, Jews section details beyond the One Hundred Associates.

Article gives Theodoric's invasion in 489; the Ostrogoths entry (same batch) says 488, so no invasion year is given here. Left out the name etymology debate, Gregory of Tours references, the Rhutenes plate, Hildebrandslied. Desc says Odoacer sent the imperial regalia to Constantinople; article says the Senate sent the insignia to Zeno, so I attribute it to the Senate.

Entry says the town was founded as Yaitsky Gorodok; the article names it Yaitsk (1613), so I used Yaitsk and no other name. Article's population, sports and notable-people sections left out. The article is short: substance is about 260 words.

Entry says the Alans withdrew after Mongol and Timurid invasions; the article mentions only the Mongols. Left out genetics, demographics tables, modern conflicts detail, diaspora, Jassic and Asud peoples, music.

Article's lead says 'disbanded in 1930'; left out. Left out ethnic breakdown of staff, rank system, directorate lists, foreign assassination list apart from Trotsky, intelligence activities, Spanish Civil War, Xinjiang.
Article has almost nothing on Aksum's stelae beyond the 520-ton broken stele; the entry's 33 m Aksum figure is the entry's own and was not repeated.
Article gives no date for the Dutch capture and burning of Olinda (entry says 1631); left out. Article mentions the 1637 governor's landing at Recife only.

Article gives civilisation span variously (1400-400 BC, 1200-400 BC); origin of the civilisation proper left unstated to avoid contradicting the entry's c. 1200 BCE. The article says La Venta moved in the 10th century BC in lead and c. 900 BC in the La Venta section; used 900 BCE.
Article gives 35 BC for the Roman colony, matching the entry's c. 35 BCE.
Entry says narrowest 'about four kilometres'; matches. Skipped marine biology detail beyond salinity.

Article says the French occupied Oujda in 1844 and 1859; entry says the French defeated the Moroccan army at Isly 1844 and occupied in 1907. Left 1844 occupation out. Population figure (2024 census) left out.
Article says Japan invaded Indochina 1940; entry begins with the oil embargo of 1941 (not in article); not repeated.
Article says capital of the Argentine Confederation 1854-1861; entry says 1853-1861: start year left out. Article is thin (about 250 words of substance, much of it climate); history is brief.
Article gives 6 June 1944 matching entry.
Entry says the duchy was ruled by a Přemyslid branch; not in the article, not repeated.
Entry's Charlemagne/Avars campaign is not in the article; article says only that the Franks invaded in the 790s. Not repeated beyond that.
Entry says Ascension Cathedral completed 1905; article gives the cathedral as 1904. Year left out.
Entry says 813 martyrs; article says about 800 beheaded. Used article's figure with 'about'; entry's 813 unrepeated.
Article says delta begins from Cairo and lists Cairo as a delta city; entry's Saladin/Ayyubid claim is not in the article and was not repeated. Omitted the 2019 find dates and wildlife.
Left out recent uses per present-day rule.

Article says Brunei ceded southern Palawan to Spain in 1749; entry says Spain extended control in the nineteenth century. 1749 cession left out. Skipped politics, tourism figures and 2019-2021 proposals.
Entry says Japan handed them nominally to Azad Hind; not in the article, left out. Population given 36,844 and 36,842 in article; used 36,844.
Entry says the Nogai Horde formed from the 15th century; article gives no date; left out. Entry says they are Sunni Muslims; not in article, not repeated.
SKIPPED: article has under about 250 words of substance on history; mostly lists, transport and recent economy plans

Article spells battle village Kerreri; entry says Karari. Article says September 1898; entry says 2 September 1898 (article gives no day). Article is thin; left out 2008 and 2023-25 events and airport details.

Article's Ur-Nammu/Ibbi-Sin dating (c. 1950 BC) not used. Ziggurat 58 by 39 m (Ashurbanipal period) vs 39 by 58 m for Ur-Gur ziggurat: only the former printed as given. Wording of Ur-Nammu left to desc.
Hairun murder undated in source. Population figures omitted (present-day). Maluku sectarian conflict 1999 left out as recent.
Skipped Putin/Russian involvement figures, US involvement, and later Russian use of the term. Dioxin poisoning 'face remains disfigured' omitted as present tense.
Article calls it also Röhm purge / Operation Hummingbird; omitted. Desc says 'at least 85', article agrees.

Article puts ancient Nuceria Alfaterna in Nocera Superiore, desc says Nocera Inferiore stands on the site: left out the siting and Hannibal/Pompeii. Castle founding date 9th vs 10th century inconsistent in article: omitted. Notable people list has no stated birthplace dates: Sannazzaro and Solimena listed as notable people; softened to 'natives' - check.
Desc: risings suppressed by 1071 vs article 'not secure until after 1072' (Treaty of Abernethy 1072): omitted the latter. Christmas Day coronation not in the article.
Present-day matters kept to lasting facts. Article says 'Gorizia Montesanto railway station also named Nova Gorica': omitted. Slovenia joined Schengen not in article.
Article does not mention the Neutral Confederacy as occupying the banks nor a date; desc's 1650 not repeated. Four sections count: Setting, History, today.
Desc's 'Burgundian kingdom destroyed in 436' is not in the article: omitted. Article says 37 manuscripts in one place and 36 in another: used 37 once.
Article's 'Mulroney subsequently negotiated two supplemental agreements with Bush' garbled; left out. Chapter on Trump-era policy omitted as recent politics.
Desc: 'ruled 615 to 683' agrees. Article contradicts itself on Sak K'uk' (daughter of Janaab Pakal I, reign 612-615 vs Pakal's mother): omitted details of dynasty. Visitor numbers, 2022 find omitted.
Present-day threats (oil exploration, climate projections), visitor numbers omitted.

Article gives conflicting populations (100,000 in 18th century vs 80,000 in 1750) and capital of Minas Gerais from 1720; desc says capital of the Captaincy: used 'capital of Minas Gerais'. World Heritage year (1980) not in article.

Article's evaluative claims (unprecedented, 'one of most influential') and press-freedom ranking left out; legacy sentence neutral. Phuc resigned 2023 not printed. 2021 relief from presidency date used.
Article says nave of the basilica was destroyed in 2016; desc says badly damaged: only 'heavy damage' stated. Saints' twin status as in article ('twin saints'); desc says sister.

Article says extinct around 1850 (Walter Sutherland, d. about 1850), claims of 1932, and speakers repeating sentences in 1894; desc says died out by the 18th century: left out extinction date and Sutherland, kept 'late 18th century' as article's 'more likely'.

Dating of walls: 4th century BC refounding vs 5th century BC in sights list: used the former once only. Article says 'mid-16th century' State of Presides; desc says from 1557: not printed. Franco-Spanish War 1635-1659 year of battle not stated: omitted.
Desc says 976 Leopold of Babenberg Austria: not in article, omitted. 'Excluded the Bavarian line' per lead; revolt details sparse. Date Otto II's marriage 14 April 972 given by article.

Death date 23 vs 24 January 1002 inconsistent in article: omitted. Desc says Congress of Gniezno 1000 and archbishopric: article only gives pilgrimage in December 999; archbishopric not in article. Place of death: 'Castle Paterno in Faleria' vs 'near Civita Castellana': used latter.
Short article: about 330 words kept; present-day sports omitted. Desc says passed to Sweden then Russia: article does not state; not repeated.

Article says spoken 'late 8th to mid-14th centuries'; entry says ninth to fourteenth, so I gave no start date. Entry calls the Oaths of Strasbourg the earliest surviving text; article says the Reichenau and Kassel glosses (8th-9th c.) come before them, so I said 'among the earliest'.
